chapters.title: Hannah's Prayer for a Son
chapters.synopsis: Hannah, barren and grieved, weeps and vows before the Lord at Shiloh that if He grants her a son she will give him back to the Lord's service. The priest blesses her, mistaking her silent prayer for drunkenness, and the Lord remembers her. Hannah bears Samuel and, once weaned, brings him to Shiloh to be raised in the tabernacle.

chapters.title: Hannah's Song; Eli's Wicked Sons
chapters.synopsis: Hannah offers a song of thanksgiving praising the Lord who raises up the poor and brings low the proud. Meanwhile Eli's sons abuse their priestly office and take sacrifices meant for the Lord by force, while young Samuel grows in favor before Him. A man of God warns Eli that his sons' wickedness will bring judgment on his entire priestly house.

chapters.title: The Lord Calls Samuel
chapters.synopsis: The young Samuel, ministering under Eli at Shiloh, hears his name called in the night and mistakes the Lord's voice for Eli's until the old priest recognizes what is happening and tells him how to answer. The Lord confirms to Samuel that judgment will fall on Eli's house for his sons' sins. Samuel grows, and all Israel comes to know him as a prophet of the Lord.

chapters.title: The Ark Captured; Eli Dies
chapters.synopsis: Israel is defeated by the Philistines and, hoping the ark of the covenant will save them, brings it into camp, only to be routed again as the ark is captured and Eli's two sons are killed. When Eli hears the ark is taken he falls backward and dies, and his daughter-in-law names her newborn son Ichabod, for the glory has departed from Israel.

segments.note: Israel is defeated; the ark of God is captured

chapters.title: The Ark Among the Philistines
chapters.synopsis: The Philistines set the captured ark in the temple of their god Dagon at Ashdod, but each morning find Dagon's image fallen before it, at last broken in pieces. The Lord afflicts the Philistine cities with tumors wherever the ark is carried, and the people cry out in terror as the plague spreads from city to city.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: The ark topples Dagon and afflicts the Philistines

chapters.title: The Ark Returns to Israel
chapters.synopsis: After seven months the Philistine priests advise sending the ark back with a guilt offering of golden images, setting it on a new cart drawn by untended cows to test whether Israel's God caused their plagues. The cows go straight to Beth-shemesh, and the Israelites rejoice, but some men look into the ark and are struck down for their irreverence.

chapters.title: Samuel Leads Israel to Repentance
chapters.synopsis: The ark rests at Kirjath-jearim for twenty years while Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods and serve the Lord alone. At Mizpah Samuel offers sacrifice and prays as the Philistines advance, and the Lord thunders against them, routing their army so decisively that Samuel raises a stone called Ebenezer, 'the Lord helped us.' Samuel judges Israel faithfully all his days.

chapters.title: Israel Demands a King
chapters.synopsis: In Samuel's old age the elders of Israel, unhappy with his corrupt sons as judges, demand a king to rule them like other nations. Samuel warns them plainly of the cost such a king will exact from their sons, daughters, fields, and flocks. The Lord tells Samuel that the people have rejected Him, not Samuel, but to heed their voice and grant their request.

chapters.title: Saul Meets Samuel
chapters.synopsis: Saul, a tall and handsome Benjamite, searches for his father's lost donkeys and comes at his servant's suggestion to consult the seer Samuel. The Lord has already told Samuel that this very man will be sent to save Israel from the Philistines. Samuel honors Saul with a place at the feast and speaks privately with him, preparing him for what is to come.

chapters.title: Saul Anointed King
chapters.synopsis: Samuel privately anoints Saul with oil and gives him three confirming signs, promising the Spirit of the Lord will come upon him and turn him into another man. The signs are fulfilled and Saul prophesies among a company of prophets, astonishing those who know him. At Mizpah Saul is chosen by lot before all Israel, though he hides among the baggage, and Samuel proclaims the manner of the kingdom.

chapters.title: Saul Delivers Jabesh-gilead
chapters.synopsis: When the Ammonites threaten to gouge out the right eye of every man in Jabesh-gilead as the price of a treaty, Saul is stirred by the Spirit of the Lord and summons all Israel to battle by cutting up oxen and sending the pieces throughout the land. Saul's army delivers Jabesh-gilead with a decisive victory, and the people renew Saul's kingdom at Gilgal with sacrifices before the Lord.

chapters.title: Samuel's Farewell Address
chapters.synopsis: Samuel, now old, reviews before Israel his years of faithful, uncorrupt service as judge, and none can accuse him of wrongdoing. He recounts the Lord's mighty deliverances from Egypt onward and calls down thunder and rain in wheat harvest as a sign that asking for a king was a great evil in the Lord's sight. Samuel nonetheless urges Israel to fear and serve the Lord faithfully, promising he will continue to pray for them.

chapters.title: Saul's Unlawful Sacrifice
chapters.synopsis: As the Philistines mass at Michmash and Israel's army scatters in fear, Saul grows impatient waiting for Samuel and offers a burnt offering himself, though only a priest should. Samuel arrives moments later and rebukes Saul, declaring that his kingdom will not continue because of his disobedience. Israel is left nearly disarmed, since the Philistines controlled the region's blacksmiths, and Philistine raiders spread through the land unopposed.

chapters.title: Jonathan's Daring Attack
chapters.synopsis: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb alone to a Philistine garrison, trusting that the Lord can save by many or by few, and their surprise attack throws the whole camp into panic that Israel exploits into a rout. Saul's rash oath forbidding food until evening nearly costs Jonathan his life when he unknowingly tastes honey, but the people intervene and rescue him from his father's vow.

chapters.title: Saul Rejected as King
chapters.synopsis: The Lord commands Saul through Samuel to destroy Amalek utterly for its ancient cruelty to Israel, but Saul spares king Agag and the best of the flocks, claiming they were kept for sacrifice. Samuel confronts Saul, declaring that to obey is better than sacrifice and that because Saul has rejected the Lord's word, the Lord rejects him from being king. Samuel himself slays Agag before the Lord at Gilgal.

chapters.title: David Anointed and Brought to Saul
chapters.synopsis: The Lord sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint one of Jesse's sons as king, and looking past the elder sons' stature, the Lord chooses David, the youngest, for the Lord looks on the heart rather than outward appearance. The Spirit of the Lord comes upon David from that day, while an evil spirit troubles Saul, and David is brought to court to soothe the king with his harp.

chapters.title: David and Goliath
chapters.synopsis: The Philistine champion Goliath taunts Israel's army for forty days, and none dare face him until young David arrives with provisions for his brothers and hears the giant's defiance of the living God. David tells Saul that the Lord, who delivered him from lion and bear, will deliver him from the Philistine, and refusing armor, he fells Goliath with a sling and stone and cuts off his head. The Philistines flee, and Saul asks whose son this young man is.

chapters.title: David and Jonathan's Covenant
chapters.synopsis: Jonathan's soul is knit to David's, and the two make a covenant of friendship as Jonathan strips off his robe and armor to give to David. Saul's jealousy grows as the women sing that David has slain his ten thousands, and he begins to fear and plot against David. David nonetheless behaves wisely in all his ways and marries Saul's daughter Michal, who loves him.

chapters.title: Saul Seeks to Kill David
chapters.synopsis: Jonathan intercedes for David and briefly reconciles him to Saul, but the king's jealousy soon returns, and he tries to pin David to the wall with a javelin. Saul's daughter Michal helps David escape through a window by night, and David flees to Samuel at Ramah, where Saul's pursuing messengers fall to prophesying instead of capturing him.

chapters.title: David and Jonathan's Covenant Renewed
chapters.synopsis: David and Jonathan devise a plan to test whether Saul truly intends to kill David, using David's absence from a feast as a signal. Saul's fury at the feast, even hurling his spear at his own son, proves David's danger is real. Jonathan warns David in the field with prearranged arrows, and the two part in tears, renewing their covenant of friendship before the Lord.

chapters.title: David Flees to Nob and Gath
chapters.synopsis: Fleeing Saul, David comes to the priests at Nob, where he receives shewbread for his hunger and the sword of Goliath, which he had left there. He then flees to Achish, king of Gath, but fearing for his life among the Philistines, feigns madness, scratching at the gate and letting spittle fall on his beard until Achish sends him away.

chapters.title: The Cave of Adullam; Doeg's Massacre
chapters.synopsis: David gathers a band of the distressed and discontented at the cave of Adullam, and places his parents in Moab for safety. Saul, enraged that the priests at Nob helped David, orders their slaughter, which his own guard refuses but a foreign herdsman carries out, killing eighty-five priests and the inhabitants of Nob. Only Abiathar the priest escapes and joins David.

chapters.title: David Delivers Keilah
chapters.synopsis: David inquires of the Lord and delivers the city of Keilah from a Philistine raid, but learns the people would betray him to Saul and flees into the wilderness of Ziph. There Jonathan finds David and strengthens his hand in God, reaffirming that David will be king and he himself will serve under him. Saul nearly traps David near Maon, but is called away by a Philistine invasion.

chapters.title: David Spares Saul at En-gedi
chapters.synopsis: Saul enters a cave at En-gedi to relieve himself, not knowing David and his men are hiding within, and David secretly cuts off a corner of Saul's robe rather than kill the Lord's anointed. Afterward David calls out to Saul, showing the piece of robe as proof he means no harm, and Saul weeps, acknowledging that David is more righteous than he and will surely become king.

chapters.title: Samuel's Death; Nabal and Abigail
chapters.synopsis: Samuel dies and all Israel mourns him. When a wealthy but churlish man refuses to reward David's men for protecting his flocks, David sets out in anger to destroy his household, but the man's wise wife intercepts David with generous gifts and pleads for restraint, turning aside his wrath. Struck by her words, the man dies of a seizure ten days later, and David takes the woman as his wife.

chapters.title: David Spares Saul Again
chapters.synopsis: David and a companion slip into Saul's camp by night while the whole army sleeps, and David again refuses to kill the Lord's anointed, taking only Saul's spear and water jug as proof of how close he came. From a distance David calls out to Saul's commander and to Saul himself, and Saul again confesses his fault, blessing David and acknowledging that he will prevail.

chapters.title: David Takes Refuge with Achish
chapters.synopsis: Weary of Saul's pursuit, David takes refuge among the Philistines under Achish, king of Gath, who grants him the town of Ziklag to dwell in. From there David raids nearby raiding peoples, letting Achish believe he is attacking Israel's own territory, and so keeps his true loyalties hidden while surviving among Israel's enemies.

segments.note: David takes refuge among the Philistines at Ziklag

chapters.title: Saul Consults the Witch of Endor
chapters.synopsis: As the Philistines gather for battle, Achish enlists David's men in his army, but David's true loyalty is soon tested. Forsaken by the Lord, who no longer answers by dream or prophet, Saul in desperation seeks out a medium at Endor, though he himself had banned such practices. Samuel's spirit is called up and pronounces that Saul and his sons will die the next day, and Saul collapses in terror.

chapters.title: The Philistines Distrust David
chapters.synopsis: As the Philistine army mobilizes for battle against Israel, the other Philistine lords object to David's presence, fearing he will turn against them in the fight to regain favor with Saul. Achish reluctantly agrees and sends David and his men back to Ziklag, sparing David the impossible choice of fighting against his own people.

chapters.title: David Recovers Ziklag
chapters.synopsis: David returns to find Ziklag burned by Amalekite raiders and all the families, including his own wives, taken captive. David inquires of the Lord and pursues the raiders, finding an abandoned Egyptian servant who guides him to their camp. David overtakes the Amalekites, recovers everyone and everything taken, and generously shares the spoil even with those too exhausted to fight.

chapters.title: The Death of Saul
chapters.synopsis: The Philistines press Israel hard on mount Gilboa, wounding Saul severely, and rather than fall into enemy hands he takes his own life, and Jonathan and his brothers die in the same battle. The men of Jabesh-gilead, remembering Saul's earlier deliverance of their city, make a night journey to recover the bodies from the wall of Beth-shan and give them honorable burial.
